This petition is filed by the petitioner U/s.166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- with interest from the date of petition till its realization for injuries sustained by him in the Motor Vehicle Accident.

. The brief case of the petitioner is as under:
On 13.08.2020 at about 5.30 pm., the petitioner was proceeding as a pillion rider on the TVS Heavy Duty Moped bearing reg.No.KA-50-K-3655 along with his grand mother Smt.Gangamma and the said moped was riding by his father Ramanjinappa on the left side of Gudibande- Gowribidanur road, near Lakkasandra gate, Gowribidanur road, near Lakkasandra gate, driver of the car bearing No.KA-40-A-9275 came with high speed and in a rash and negligent manner without following traffic rules and regulations, all of a sudden came from back side and dashed against the petitioner's moped from behind.
Due to impact petitioner, his grand mother and his father were thrown out from the moped and sustained severe head and bodily injuries.

Immediately after the accident, petitioner was shifted to Govt., General Hospital,
Gowribidanur wherein first aid was done, then he was shifted to Someshwara hospital, (SCCH-9) 4 MVC.No.3625/2021 Gowribidanur wherein the petitioner was treated as inpatient and underwent wound debridement.
The petitioner was 4 years at the time of accident.
The Gowribidanur rural police have registered a criminal case against the driver of the car bearing No.KA-40-A- 9275 in crime No.0207/2020 under Section 279,337 and 304A of IPC.
The respondent No.2 being the RC owner and respondent No.1 being the insurer are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
3. After service of summons, the respondent No.2 has not appeared before the court hence, placed exparte and respondent No.1 has appeared before the tribunal and filed its written statement.

sentences.text: The brief contents of written statement of respondent No.1 is that, the claim petition is not maintainable in law or on facts.
It has admitted the issuance of the policy in favour of the respondent No.2.
Respondent No.1 has denied the involvement of the car (SCCH-9) 5 MVC.No.3625/2021 bearing reg.No.KA-40-A-9275 in the alleged accident.

It has denied the age,
occupation, income and amount spent by the petitioner.

Further deposed that, the owner of the vehicle did not report and furnished the RTO documents pertaining to the offending vehicle regarding the driving licence of the person who was driving the vehicle at the time of accident which required under Section 134(C) and the concerned police have not complied the mandatory provisions of Sec.158(6) of MV Act.
It has contented that, at the time of accident, petitioner was not wearing safety headgear which is clear violation of MV Act.
There are three persons are traveling on the motor cycle against to its seating capacity and lost control over the same and caused the accident.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive, exorbitant and exaggerated.
With these grounds the respondent No.1 sought for rejecting the claim petition.
5. On the basis of above pleadings, this Tribunal (SCCH-9) 6 MVC.No.3625/2021 has framed the following issues:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner prove that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the accident occurred on 13-08-2020 at about 5.30 p.m., near Lakkasandra gate, on Gudibande Gowribidanuru road, Gowribidanuru Taluk, Chickballapura due to rash and negligent driving of car bearing registration No.KA-40-A-9275 by its driver as alleged in the petition?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount and from whom?
3. What Order or Award?
6. In order to prove his case, the father of the petitioner himself examined as PW.1 and in all got marked documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P.9.

7. Heard arguments and perused the materials available on record.
8.

My answer to the above issues are as under:-
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative;
Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative;

Issue No.1:- It is the case of the PW-1 that, on 13.08.2020 at about 5.30 pm., he was riding the TVS Heavy Duty Moped bearing reg.No.KA-50-K-3655 along with his mother Smt.Gangamma and petitioner as his pillion riders on the left side of Gudibande-Gowribidanur road, near Lakkasandra gate, Gowribidanur road, near Lakkasandra gate, driver of the car bearing No.KA-40-A- 9275 came with high speed and in a rash and negligent manner without following traffic rules and regulations,
all of a sudden came from back side and dashed against the petitioner's moped from behind.
Due to impact petitioner thrown out from the moped and sustained severe head and bodily injuries.

10. In order to prove the case, the petitioner himself examined as PW1 and filed affidavit in lieu of (SCCH-9) 8 MVC.No.3625/2021 chief-examination and reiterated all the facts mentioned in the petition.

He also got marked Ex.P1 to Ex.P.9 which are FIR, statement, mahazar, wound certificate,
IMV report, charge sheet, discharge summary, adhar card, medical bills statements.
11. On perusal of police documents which are marked at Ex-P1 to Ex-P6 it is clear that the accident took place on 13-08-2020 at about 5.30 p.m., and
Ex . P.1
- FIR in crime No.0207/2020 came to be registered on 13-08- 2020 i.e., on the same of accident at Gowribidanur Police Station for the offences punishable u/s 279, 337, 304A of IPC.
Ex.P.2 - complaint lodged by PW-1 on 13-08-2020.

Ex.P.3 is the panchanama, Ex.P4 is the wound certificate, Ex.P5 is the IMV report, Ex.P6 is the charge sheet which describe the spot of accident as towards Gowribidanur, Gudibande road, D palya cross, near Lakkasandra gate and Ex.P.7 is the discharge summary, Ex.P.5 is the IMV report which shows the damages caused the vehicles (SCCH-9) 9 MVC.No.3625/2021 which involved in the alleged accident I.e., motor cycle bearing No.KA-50-K-3655 and car bearing No.KA-40-A- 9295.

Ex.P.6 is the charge sheet which has been filed against the driver of car bearing No.KA-40-A-9275.
12.
The learned counsel for the respondent No.1 has cross examined PW-1.
I have perused the entire cross- examination of PW-1.

In his cross-examination he has specifically denied the suggestions made by the learned counsel for the respondent regarding negligence of driver of the car bearing No.KA-40-A-9275, the alleged accident occurred.
The learned counsel for the respondent No.1 has not elicited anything from the mouth of PW-1 to disbelieve his version.
There is nothing on record to show that the charge-sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.

Therefore, on over all appreciation of evidence, I am of the opinion that the accident occurred due to sole negligence of driver of the offending car bearing No.KA-40-A-9275 which belongs to the respondent No.2 and respondent (SCCH-9) 10 MVC.No.3625/2021 No.1 is its insurer.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
13. Issue No.2:- This petition is filed for seeking compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by the petitioner in the road traffic accident as stated above.
The petitioner has already proved that, the accident was occurred due to sole negligence on the part of driver of the offending Car bearing reg.No.KA-40-A-9275.

PW.1 has produced wound certificate which reveals petitioner had sustained CLW over right side of forehead measuring 6 x 2 x 1 cm, abrasion over right maxillary area 4 x 2 x 2 cms, laceration of upper lip right side 2 x 1 x 1 cm and the said injuries are described as simple in nature and Ex-P7 discharge summary issued by the Someshwara Hospital which reveals that in the hospital diagnosed sutured wound on right eye brow and forehead and in the said hospital sutures removal, wound debridement and revision suturing of over right eye brow with 4-0 Lokesh Alias Lokesh Babu vs Shri Ram Gen Ins Co Ltd on 19 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51341245/
4 ethilon done under sedation (SCCH-9) 11 MVC.No.3625/2021 and local anaestesia and he took treatment as inpatient from 13-8-2020 to 19-8-2020. i.e., for 7 days.

sentences.text: The petitioner has not examined the doctor and also not produced any disability certificate to show that he is suffering from physical disability.
Therefore in view of the non production of disability certificate and doctor evidence, it can not be considered as the petitioner is having any disability due to the accidental injury.
The petitioner has produced ex-P9-8 medical bills for Rs.20,050/-.
Further the parents of the petitioner may spent some amount towards food, nourishment, conveyance purpose.
Hence, by considering the treatment taken by the petitioner, it is just and proper to award the Global Compensation.
Hence, I am of the opinion that, the Global Compensation of Rs.1,00,000/- is to be awarded to the petitioner.

14. Regarding Liability: The respondent No.1 has taken contention that, at the time of accident,
petitioner was riding his vehicle without holding valid and effective (SCCH-9) 12 MVC.No.3625/2021 driving licence.
The petitioner has not produced the driving licence.
PW-1 during his cross-examination

clearly deposed that at the time of accident, he lost the driving licence,
it is not denied by the respondent.

Hence, there is no reason to believe the defence of the respondent that at the time of accident, petitioner has not holding valid and effective driving licence.
15.
Further the respondent No.1 has taken another defence that father of the petitioner was riding the vehicle without observing the movements of the vehicles.
In this regard, perused the petition wherein submitted that car/offending vehicle came with high speed from his behind in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motor cycle.
Further after investigation, IO has filed final report as per Ex-P6 in support of the petitioner.

PW-1 subjected to cross-examination wherein he clearly deposed that car came in a rash and negligent manner from behind and dashed to the PW-1's motor cycle, due to (SCCH-9) 13 MVC.No.3625/2021 which accident occurred.
Further PW-1 clearly denied the suggestion that due to his rash and negligent driving accident occurred.
Hence the defence of the respondent No.1 is not believable that due to the negligence of the rider of the moped accident occurred.
16. Further respondent No.1 has taken defence that petitioner was not wearing helmet at the time of alleged accident.
PW-1 subjected to cross examination wherein learned counsel for the respondent No.1 has not put a single suggestion/question about the said defence.
Hence, mere defence taken in the written statement is not sufficient to prove the same in the absence of documentary evidence.

At this juncture, this tribunal relied upon the decision reported in - MFA No.3459/2021(MV-1) ( Sri.
Sadath Ali Khan Va. Sri. Noor Ahmed Sayeed and another) wherein it is held that - " 26.

sentences.text: However, not wearing protective headgear does not negate the right to compensation.
Courts have consistently (SCCH-9) 14 MVC.No.3625/2021 held that the compensation awarded should not be diluted solely because the injured party was not wearing protective headgear.
The principle of "just compensation" requires that while contributory negligence can be a factor in determining the amount of compensation, it should not result in an unjust reduction.
The compensation must be fair and reasonable, reflecting the actual losses and the nature of injuries sustained.

sentences.text: However, the contentious contention is taken by the Insurance Company that the claimant was not wearing the helmet.
But the Motor Vehicles Act is a beneficial legislation.

Keeping in view of the scope of Section 129 of the Act and in a given peculiar facts and circumstances of the case, the entire liability shall be fastened on respondent No.2-insurance company".
17.
By considering the above said citation, at the present case also, not wearing protective headgear does not negate the right to compensation.

(SCCH-9) 15 MVC.No.3625/2021  18. Therefore, the respondent No.2 being the R.C.Owner and the respondent No.1 being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
However, the respondent No.1 being the insurer of offending vehicle is primarily liable to pay compensation with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 answered Partly in the Affirmative.
19. ISSUE NO.3:

In view of my finding on issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following;
O R D E R
The petition filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for Global Compensation of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees one lakh only) with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondents No.1 and 2 are  jointly and severally liable to pay  (SCCH-9) 16 MVC.No.3625/2021 compensation to the petitioner.

However, in view of the policy, the respondent No.2/insurance company is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner and directed to deposit the compensation amount in this tribunal within one month from the date of this order.

In the event of deposit of the said compensation amount, 50% shall be deposited in the name of petitioner in Karnataka Bank, City Civil Court Branch, Bengaluru till he attains the age of majority and the remaining 50% shall be released in favour of father of petitioner/PW-1 on proper identification through E-payment as PW-1 spent money for the treatment of the petitioner Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
